idea_headline: A drawing set, not a document.
idea: Drafting treats every page as a numbered sheet from an engineering drawing set: a gridded vellum, a frame, a title block, and the subject drawn in line-work with its dimensions. The reader is handed something measured. Cobalt annotates; vermilion marks the revision.
use_for: Implementation plans, specs and RFCs, process explainers, product teardowns, scroll stories where one object comes apart or goes together.
avoid_when: Warm or emotional subjects, consumer marketing, dashboards that need many simultaneous status colours, or any page whose reader is not expected to inspect.
principles_headline: Draw the subject. Dimension it. Number the sheet.
principles: The object is drawn, not pictured.
Line-work in ink at 2px for the object and 1px for construction. Photographs are for marketing; a drawing is for understanding.
Figures attach to the thing they measure with a dimension line and arrowheads. A figure floating in a card is a rumour.
Two colours only. Cobalt for dimensions, links and the primary action; vermilion for what changed, what failed, the one part the reader must find.
A 24px grid is the page texture. Elements snap to it; margins are multiples of it.
Each major part of the page is a sheet with its own title block: number, title, revision, scale. Reading the title blocks reads the plan.
voice: Imperative and precise: "Book one slot. Refuse the second." Not "Users should be able to…"
State the unit once in the title block, then never repeat it.
Mark assumptions as assumptions, in caution; mark verified results as verified, in positive.
Revision notes say what changed and why, in one line each.
colour_headline: Ink on vellum, cobalt annotations, one vermilion revision.
colour_note: Day is a cool grey-white vellum with a visible grid. Night is the same sheet as a blueprint: Prussian ground, pale line-work, cobalt lifted to sky-blue and vermilion warmed. Status colours are for ledgers and tables, never for the drawing itself.
chart_note: Cobalt is the measured series; vermilion is the exception or the revision; ink is the baseline. Charts in Drafting look like figures: axis lines in ink, grid in the grid token, direct labels in the dim role.
type_headline: Archivo for the sheet, Plex Mono for the measurements.
type_note: Archivo at 900 in caps gives titles the weight of a stencil; at 400 it reads like a spec. Archivo Narrow carries the title-block apparatus. IBM Plex Mono carries every figure and every path.
space_headline: A 24px grid, a 12px frame, 2px for the object.
space: The drafting grid. Margins and gaps are multiples: 24, 48, 72.
edges: Everything. A drawing has no rounded corners.
Every sheet and panel is framed in 1px ink. Panels inside a sheet use the grid token instead.
The subject is drawn at 2px; construction lines, leaders and dimensions at 1px.
Closed 8px triangles in the line colour, drawn as polygons. No SVG markers.
depth: None. A sheet lies flat. Hover reveals by changing the line colour to cobalt, not by lifting.
A 2px cobalt outline, offset 2px, on every control.
A scalloped outline in vermilion around the changed region, with a REV tag.
Lines draw in (stroke-dashoffset, 600ms ease-out) on first reveal. Exploded parts translate along their axis as the reader scrolls. Reduced motion shows the finished drawing.
components_headline: The kit becomes a title block.
components_note: Kit components take Drafting through the contract: square, 1px edges, cobalt primary, vellum grounds. Authored classes add the title-block cells, the dimension figures and the revision marks.

motifs_headline: Dimension lines, revision clouds, title blocks.
motifs_note: Drafting draws with the apparatus of a drawing set. Put the data on the drawing: a count becomes a dimension, a share becomes a section, a change becomes a cloud.

motifs.title: The dimension line
motifs.usage: A measured figure attached to its object with a 1px cobalt line and 8px closed arrowheads, the figure in the dim role above the line. Use it for counts, widths, durations.

motifs.title: The revision cloud
motifs.usage: A scalloped vermilion outline around the region that changed since the last revision, with a REV tag. One cloud per sheet; if everything changed, the sheet is new.

motifs.title: The title block
motifs.usage: A framed strip of cells at the bottom of every sheet: drawing number, title, sheet x/y, scale, revision, date. Reading the title blocks reads the plan.

dos: Draw the subject in ink line-work and attach every figure with a dimension line.
Frame every sheet and give it a title block.
Cobalt for annotation, vermilion for the one revision.
Snap to the 24px grid; let it show.
donts: No photographs as the hero; no rounded corners; no shadows.
No status colour on the drawing itself.
No floating numbers; a figure without a leader is a rumour.
No more than one revision cloud per sheet.
binding_losses: The grid texture, the dimension and arrowhead styles, the title block and the revision cloud have no contract slot; they are d-* classes and inline SVG. Kit tables take the grid rules and mono figures but not the narrow caps header.
footer: Vellum first, Blueprint second. Fonts: Archivo 400/500/700/900, Archivo Narrow 500/700, IBM Plex Mono 400/500/700, all Google-hosted.

queries.series: select path, phones from rows order by phones desc
queries.table: select path, phones, share, state from rows order by phones desc
queries.totals: select sum(phones) as total, max(case when path = 'Back in use' then phones end) as reuse, max(case when path = 'Donor for parts' then phones end) as donor, max(case when path = 'Recycled' then phones end) as recycle from rows

data.tab_body: Sheet 1: the subject in plan with overall dimensions.

hand.headline: Line-work, dimensioned, on the grid.
hand.note: Drafting draws the subject the way a drawing set would: the object in 1.5px ink line-work with square caps, nothing filled, construction at 1px, and cobalt only for the dimension or the one part being measured. Vermilion marks the revision. A drawing without a figure attached to it is unfinished.
rules: 1.5px ink for the object, square caps and mitred joins. 1px grid lines for construction.
None. Cobalt as an outline marks the measured part; vermilion marks the revised one.
Dimension figures in the mono dim role, attached with a 1px cobalt leader and closed arrowheads.
Lines draw in (stroke-dashoffset, 600ms ease-out) on first reveal; exploded parts translate along their axis.

motion: The frame turns cobalt, 120ms. Nothing lifts.
The fill inverts to ink for the press. No scale.
A 2px cobalt outline offset 2px on every control.
Line-work draws in over 600ms with stroke-dashoffset; text appears complete.
Exploded parts translate along one axis as the reader scrolls; the sticky figure is the template's job.
Bars grow from the axis over 300ms; figures count up in the dim role.

tpl.slide_title: One slot per machine per hour.
tpl.slide_sub: The database decides who wins a contested slot; the interface only reports it.
tpl.slide_body: Of 100 returned units, this many went back into service after inspection. The remainder were harvested or recycled, as dimensioned on sheet 3.
tpl.ed_deck: A partial unique index on (equipment, slot) is the whole concurrency story. The second request to arrive gets a 409 and the next free hour. Here is the sequence, dimensioned.
tpl.ed_byline: Drawn by the platform team · Rev B · 2 Oct 2026
tpl.ed_body: Two requests for the same slot arrive within twenty milliseconds. Both pass the availability check, because the check reads a snapshot. Both attempt the insert. The index admits one row; the second insert fails with a unique violation that the API translates into a 409 and a suggestion. The user who lost never sees a success message that is later withdrawn.
steps: Each square is one unit, drawn in plan. Inspection sorts them into three paths within a shift.
Sixty go back into service, twenty-five are opened for parts, fifteen are recycled. Every count is a dimension on the sheet.

tpl.landing_sub: Specs, plans and explainers drawn as a numbered drawing set: the subject in line-work, every figure attached to the thing it measures, revisions clouded.
features: The subject is line-work the reader can inspect, with dimensions attached.
Each section is a sheet with a title block: number, title, scale, revision.
What changed is circled in vermilion with a REV tag. One cloud per sheet.
